payload.methodNotes: The talk frames forward deployed engineering as a go-to-market model for selling technical software to non-technical buyers, but only when the company can anchor that work in a reusable platform. I treated the transcript as the only evidence source, so the record stays close to the speaker's own claims about when the model works, what its maintenance tradeoffs are, and how AI changes the landscape. I avoided turning examples into general facts unless the speaker explicitly used them to support the method.

payload.summary: The talk argues that forward deployed engineering is not just custom services with a new name; it is a design-partnership motion scaled into the enterprise. The core mechanism is to sell outcomes by having customer-facing engineers build on shared platform primitives, so the company can solve customer problems without recreating the software stack from scratch for every account. The main tradeoff is maintenance: if the work is not anchored in a reusable platform, the function collapses into a dev shop that is expensive, hard to staff, and impossible to sustain. The practical advice is to adopt FDE only when you truly need to sell technical capability to non-technical buyers, and to use custom projects as a way to discover which parts of the product should later be generalized.
